papers.title: Segre Classification as a Framework for Generating Exact Solutions in Static Cylindrical Spacetimes with Levi-Civita Matching
papers.abstract: The main objective of this article is to analyze cylindrically symmetric static spacetime based on the Segre classification, where each Segre type corresponds to a set of canonical forms of Ricci spinors represented by Newman-Penrose scalars. The surviving Segre types of trace-free Ricci tensor in the cylindrical geometry are $[1,(111)]$, $[1,1(11)]$, $[(1,1)11]$, $[1,111]$, $[(1,11)1]$, $[(1,1)(11)]$ and $[(1,111)]$. Different combinations of eigenvalues and eigenvectors formed via Segre classification aid in understanding the distribution of matter and energy within that particular kind. Solutions are presented for the isotropic type $[1,(111)]$, for the anisotropic type $[1,1(11)]$, where a new metric function is introduced, and for type $[1,111]$, where all three pressures differ and the Krori-Barua functions are used. They satisfy the physical and stability criteria, namely the Zeldovich condition, causality condition, energy conditions and adiabatic index. The types $[(1,1)11]$ and $[(1,11)1]$ have $\rho=-P_r$ and give dark energy like configurations in which the strong energy condition is violated in the core, the latter having the tachyonic fluid form of the energy momentum tensor. For type $[(1,1)(11)]$, a charged solution in the presence of a non-null electromagnetic field is obtained and joined to an electrovac exterior. Matching with the Levi-Civita exterior shows that the vanishing of the radial pressure at the boundary is equivalent to the Darmois conditions. The C-energy and the curvature invariants are evaluated for each solution, and the results are compared with earlier works.

papers.title: Continuum Pumping Revises Metallicity in the Orion Nebula
papers.abstract: The enrichment of heavy elements in the interstellar medium is central to understanding galaxy evolution. Oxygen, the most abundant element after H and He, provides the principal tracer of gas-phase metallicity, typically measured using nebular emission lines in star-forming regions. However, a long-standing issue-the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF)-produces a $\sim 0.25$ dex offset between metallicities derived from recombination lines (RLs) and collisionally excited lines (CELs). We present deep spectroscopic observations of the Orion Nebula (M42), and use them to assess the contribution of the often neglected continuum pumping process. We find that the continuum pumping effect is at least a factor of two stronger than previously expected. After accounting for the flux contribution from continuum pumping, the RL metallicity is consistent with the CEL metallicity, thus explaining the bulk of the ADF. Reassessing O/H measurements in five literature star-forming regions using the same method, we similarly find a systematic reduction of RL-based metallicities. These results indicate that RL metallicities, which have previously been considered more reliable than CELs, are subject to potentially large bias from continuum pumping. This study provides a foundation to correct this bias and establish accurate element abundance scales throughout cosmic time.

papers.title: Revisiting Evidence of Temperature Fluctuations in H II Regions. I. Interionic temperature differences
papers.abstract: The oxygen abundance of H II regions is a fundamental tracer of chemical enrichment and gas cycling and is now routinely measured across a broad range of cosmic time. A persistent complication is the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF): the O$^{++}$/H$^+$ abundance inferred from optical recombination lines (RLs) is systematically higher than that inferred from collisionally excited lines (CELs). Small-scale temperature fluctuations within the O$^{++}$-emitting gas are among the most widely discussed explanations for this discrepancy. However, the recent identification of a substantial continuum-pumping contribution to the O II spectrum of M42 motivates a renewed assessment of which observations uniquely favor a temperature-based interpretation and which are also compatible with other mechanisms. In this first paper of a series, I examine the relation between the inferred temperature-fluctuation parameter, $t^2$, and interionic temperature differences, focusing on $\Delta T_e=T_e([OIII])-T_e([NII])$. Photoionization calculations show that ionization stratification naturally produces systematic temperature differences between the low- and high-ionization zones. Meanwhile, the conversion from an ADF to $t^2$ is strongly temperature dependent because CEL emissivities are nonlinear functions of electron temperature. I show that these two effects can account for much of the observed $t^2$-$\Delta T_e$ relation without requiring the interionic temperature difference itself to trace fluctuations within the O$^{++}$ zone. This result does not exclude temperature fluctuations in H II regions. Instead, it indicates that interionic temperature differences should be interpreted with care and, on their own, provide limited discrimination among proposed origins of the ADF.

papers.title: The MeerKAT absorption line survey: Galactic OH absorption at 18 cm
papers.abstract: We present a blind search for Galactic OH 18-cm absorption lines towards 19,130 radio sources brighter than 1mJy at 1.4GHz, using 390 pointings of the MeerKAT Absorption Line Survey (MALS). We apply an automated line search followed by Bayesian nested sampling to identify OH 1667MHz, 1665MHz and 1612MHz absorption features, using HI emission and absorption profiles as physically motivated priors. We identify 15 confident detections of OH 1667/1665 MHz absorption. The majority of detections are associated with a visual extinction ($A_{\rm V}$) excess and, within the same MALS pointings, with detected CO emission and a high incidence rate of HI absorption, consistent with OH tracing the H$_2$-bearing medium. We also identify 9 candidates of OH 1612MHz satellite line absorption, two of which coincide with OH main line detections and show integrated optical depth ratios well above the LTE expectation of 1:9. As in previous studies, $N(\rm OH)$ shows no dependence on $N$(HI). Accounting for the varying sensitivity across sight lines, we estimate the covering fraction of OH-bearing gas at $\log N(\rm OH) > 12$ to be $C = 0.051 \pm 0.008$, providing an independent and a more precise estimate than previous measurements of the diffuse molecular gas. We also find qualitative evidence for a decrease of the covering fraction with Galactic latitude. Stacking reveals a clear OH absorption signal that becomes increasingly prominent when sight lines are weighted by $A_{\rm V}$ excess, independently confirming the association of OH with diffuse molecular gas. Modeling of the physical conditions yields hydrogen number densities of 10-100 cm$^{-3}$, typical H$_2$ column densities $\log N(\rm H_2) > 21$, and UV-flux to number density ratios of 0.01-0.3 Mathis cm$^{3}$, typical of the CNM.

papers.title: Deep UV Spectroscopy of an Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxy at z = 5.725
papers.abstract: We present deep X-shooter follow-up spectroscopy of AMORE6, an exceptionally metal-poor galaxy at z = 5.725. The new spectrum provides stringent upper limits on rest-frame ultraviolet metal lines, including NV, CIV, NIV], NIII], and OIII]. The non-detection of CIV breaks the density-metallicity degeneracy present in previous analyses based on the [OIII]/Hbeta ratio, excluding the high-density, chemically enriched gas scenario and strengthening the evidence for an extremely metal-poor environment. The X-shooter spectrum also reveals a narrow Lyman-alpha line with a velocity dispersion sigma_v = 23.2 +/- 0.5 km/s and a nearly symmetric profile centered at the systemic redshift measured from Hbeta. Combining the Lyman-alpha line width with the measured source size, we infer a dynamical mass M_dyn = (1-22) x 10^7 Msun, assuming that the line width traces gravitational motions. Spectral energy distribution modeling using Pop III and Pop II stellar population libraries yields stellar masses (1-5) x 10^5 Msun. Although all models reproduce the observed blue UV continuum and Halpha equivalent width (EW), none simultaneously reproduces the Hbeta luminosity and EW, with the observed Hbeta luminosity exceeding the model predictions by up to 3.7 sigma. Possible explanations include departures from standard recombination conditions or limitations in the adopted stellar population models. We discuss possible interpretations of AMORE6, including massive-star formation in an atomic-cooling halo and a gravitationally bound star cluster.

papers.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schrödinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the WKB approximation and Leaver's continued-fraction this http URL results reveal corrections to the QNM oscillation frequencies and damping rates arising from rotation, pure quantum effects, and their this http URL the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of gravitational metric perturbations in a noncommutative Kerr black hole spacetime using a Drinfeld twist, extending prior work beyond the Schwarzschild case. Our findings demonstrate that quantum deformation effects alter both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of quasinormal modes, with spin-quantum coupling introducing additional spin-dependent corrections to the Kerr QNM spectrum. Using a Kerr-anchored phenomenological prescription, we estimate the fractional frequency and damping-time shifts for selected merger remnants from the GWTC-3 and GWTC-5.0 catalogs. papers.title: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals: accessing generic orbits
papers.abstract: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRI) are a significant gravitational wave source and a target for the upcoming LISA mission. Computations of the fluxes of conserved quantities, such as energy and angular momentum, are a critical part of modeling EMRI waveforms and can be performed using a frequency domain formalism to solve the Teukolsky equation. This requires computations of large numbers of mode amplitudes, many of which are negligible. However, it is unknown ex ante which can be safely skipped. We present a machine learning approach to estimate the dominant radial mode number as a function of the remaining mode numbers and apply it to reduce the number of unnecessary computations in EMRI flux calculation.

papers.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
papers.abstract: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN) compactness parameter $1/p$, where $p$ is the dimensionless semi-latus rectum, and in the eccentricity $e$, up to 10PN and $e^{20}$, extending beyond prior 6PN and $e^{16}$ results available for generic orbits. We characterize how the PN flux coefficients depend on the black hole spin $a$ and $e$, and find a set of spin-dependent components that can be resummed as closed-form expressions in $e$. The analytical expressions are then validated with numerical comparisons against high-precision sample results from an independent Teukolsky code and with a broader set of numerically interpolated values derived from a flux data set produced with the same code. For $a=0.9M$, the numerically evaluated 10PN fluxes match current interpolated flux grids ($\sim10^{-7}$) for $p\gtrsim20$ to $75$ as $e$ ranges from $0.1$ to $0.7$, where they could replace Teukolsky-code results.

papers.title: A Cross-Domain Simulator and Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Global 21-cm Inference
papers.abstract: End-to-end uncertainty propagation in scientific inference often requires repeated evaluation of coupled simulators spanning multiple physical domains, often at prohibitive computational cost. Global 21-cm cosmology is an extreme example: a millikelvin cosmological signal must be separated from radio foregrounds and instrumental effects four orders of magnitude larger, making inference acutely sensitive to model misspecification. Reliable recovery is therefore contingent on an exceptionally accurate model that jointly propagates uncertainty through the complete observational chain. We present a differentiable, GPU-accelerated hybrid forward model combining neural emulation of the cosmological signal, a physics-informed multi-resolution parameterisation of the galactic foregrounds, and a linear surrogate model of the antenna. This unifies simulators spanning astrophysics and computational electromagnetics while reducing evaluation time by a factor of $7.2\times10^{7}$. Using GPU-accelerated Nested Slice Sampling, we benchmark the framework across 100 unseen signal realisations and find that 94 injected profiles lie entirely within their corresponding 95% credible bands. Together, the simulator and reference Nested Slice Sampling results provide a demanding benchmark of posterior calibration, mode coverage, and evidence accuracy across next-generation stochastic samplers, simulation-based inference, and variational inference frameworks.

papers.title: Interactions between the magnetised jets in the twin radio galaxy J104455+354055
papers.abstract: Pairs of galaxies in which both objects host kiloparsec-scale radio jets are extremely rare. Such systems provide unique opportunity to study the formation of relativistic jets and their resistance to side-way collisions with each other prior to their eventual merger. We analyse the radio data for the twin radio galaxy J104455+354055 associated with a pair of distant elliptical galaxies (z=0.163). The radio jets of both sources avoid disruption/merging for the initial tens of kiloparsecs. We investigate the role of the magnetic fields in the propagation of these radio jets. We used VLA radio data at high frequencies in both compact and extended array configurations to obtain sensitive high-resolution polarimetric data and study the properties of the magnetic fields in all jets. Polarisation data suggest shearing of the magnetic fields at points where the jets bend. The orientation of the magnetic field parallel to jet axis helps confine the jet. Such field configuration in two adjacent jets seems to prevent them from merging. The strength of the magnetic field slightly increases in jet bends and the associated shearing enhances the ordered component of the magnetic field. The more diffuse radio plumes at the end of each jet have comparable strengths and energies of the magnetic field. The twin radio galaxy J104455+354055 provides a unique possibility to study the interplay of radio jets of two radio galaxies. The analysis of the properties of the magnetic fields observed along the radio jets suggests that the wiggles and bends of these jets, caused by the likely interactions of the host galaxies, could be also governed by the magnetic fields that may prevent them from merging. The derived strengths and energies of the magnetic field in different parts of the jets should allow us to improve the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of radio galaxies.

papers.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
papers.abstract: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.

papers.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and Eöt-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the Eöt-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.

papers.title: Geometric distinguishability of two-source gravitational-wave signals from the extrinsic geometry of the single-source waveform manifold
papers.abstract: Overlapping gravitational-wave signals can produce strong degeneracies in which a multi-source waveform is accurately represented by a single effective source. We formulate this source-confusion problem geometrically by treating the family of single-source waveforms as an embedded manifold in the noise-weighted detector Hilbert space. We introduce the distance-to-manifold statistic, defined as the minimum residual obtained by fitting a waveform with the single-source model, and show that its squared value is directly related to the maximized likelihood difference between two-source and single-source hypotheses in the noiseless limit. For two sources with nearby parameters, perturbative minimization demonstrates that the effective single-source fit absorbs all leading tangent-space deformations. The first irreducible residual lies in the normal space of the waveform manifold and is governed by its second fundamental form. We validate our approach using a six-parameter frequency-domain inspiral model with a LISA-like time-delay-interferometry response. Direct optimization reproduces the predicted quartic scaling over the numerically resolved regime, while two-dimensional confusion-zone maps reveal strongly anisotropic distinguishability boundaries. These results establish extrinsic waveform-manifold curvature as a coordinate-independent diagnostic of local multi-source confusion and provide a practical framework for identifying parameter-space directions in which overlapping gravitational-wave sources are most difficult to resolve.

papers.title: The Science Chapter of the Einstein Telescope Geometry Comparison Report
papers.abstract: This is the Scientific Added Value Chapter of the Einstein Telescope (ET) Geometry Comparison Report, commissioned from the ET Organization by the ET Board of Governmental Representatives. We compare three configurations: a single-site 10-km triangle ($\Delta$) and two 15-km L-shaped detectors (2L) at widely separated sites, either nearly aligned or misaligned. We use metrics representative of the ET science case: compact-binary populations, dense matter, cosmography, stochastic backgrounds, multimessenger astronomy, fundamental physics, and continuous and burst sources. All three configurations deliver the ET science case, but they excel in different areas. For most sensitivity-driven science, the 2L configurations outperform the $\Delta$. The misaligned 2L is best for localizing and characterizing individual sources, multimessenger astronomy, and bright-siren cosmology. The nearly aligned 2L is best for stochastic backgrounds. The $\Delta$ localizes sources better than the aligned 2L and performs comparably to both 2L configurations for continuous and burst sources and at kilohertz frequencies. A 2L orientation of $30^\circ$ is a good compromise between stochastic-background sensitivity and localization. We validate Fisher information matrix (FIM) forecasts against Bayesian inference for $\sim550$ binary black hole and neutron star-black hole signals. Despite substantial differences, the FIM shows no systematic preference for either configuration for intrinsic parameters. For distance and sky localization, the FIM cannot capture multimodality and long-range correlations, leading to larger discrepancies, which however do not affect the ranking. Adding Cosmic Explorer to the network improves the reach of all three ET configurations, especially in volume localization and characterization of high-redshift sources. Differences between geometries shrink, but the ranking is largely unchanged.

papers.title: Redshift-space 3$\times$2pt statistics of galaxy clustering and intrinsic alignments at one-loop order
papers.abstract: Intrinsic alignments of galaxies, long regarded as a systematic in weak lensing, are now recognized as a cosmological probe complementary to galaxy clustering. Exploiting them with spectroscopic surveys requires accurate models in redshift space beyond the linear regime. In this work, we derive the galaxy density--shape cross-power spectrum and shape auto-power spectra at one-loop order in redshift space. We consider two models, one based on the effective field theory (EFT) and the other on the Taruya--Nishimichi--Saito (TNS) prescription. They share the bias expansion but differ in how they treat small-scale velocities along the line of sight. The EFT model expands the effects of these velocities perturbatively and absorbs their sensitivity to small scales into counterterms. We show that, for the sky-projected shape field, this model requires six renormalized bias parameters and two counterterms. Up to order $k^2$, the stochastic terms require two parameters for the cross spectrum and four parameters for the auto spectra. The TNS-based model keeps the one-point velocity dispersion in an unexpanded damping factor and treats it as a single free parameter. We extend our previous linear-bias TNS-based model of the cross spectrum to nonlinear bias and the shape auto spectra. We find that all loop integrals reduce to those already used for shape spectra in real space and galaxy clustering in redshift space, and we evaluate them with FFTLog. We compare both models with power spectra measured from halos in $N$-body simulations and find good agreement on mildly nonlinear scales. These models provide a basis for joint cosmological analyses of galaxy clustering and intrinsic alignments with imaging and spectroscopic galaxy surveys, in which intrinsic alignments are utilized as a cosmological probe.

papers.title: Constraining Regular Black Hole Models with the Effective Field Theory treatment of General Relativity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a method for using perturbative predictions from treating general relativity as an effective field theory to constrain non-perturbative approaches to quantum gravity in black hole contexts. We start by reviewing a known result from this framework, which estimates the first quantum corrections to the interaction energy of a static particle near a black hole. We then propose a way to test non-perturbative quantum black hole models - specifically those formulated as modified Schwarzschild metrics, also known as regular black holes - against this perturbative result. To illustrate, we apply our method to the Hayward metric, showing that it does not align with the perturbative prediction, and we identify the most general metric that can reproduce the expected result.

papers.title: Accuracy, Convergence and Consistency of Dark Matter Evolution with the PhotoNs-3 Code
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the accuracy and convergence of PhotoNs-3, a cosmological N-body code employed for the HyperMillennium simulation. In particular, we examine its convergence with respect to parameters that affect the accuracy of the force calculation and the time evolution, such as the softening length and the adaptive time-stepping scheme, and find that it converges very well. Furthermore, using GADGET as the benchmark, we design four sets of simulations to compare the mutual consistency. We compare the power spectrum of the density field, halo density profiles, and the halo and subhalo mass functions. The difference between PhotoNs-3 and the Gadget codes is at the same level as that between Gadget-3 and Gadget-4. Meanwhile, PhotoNs-3 generally achieves a significant computational speedup. This work establishes that the accuracy and reliability of PhotoNs-3 and its simulations are sufficient for Stage IV galaxy surveys.

papers.title: Cold CCH and warm CH3CCH: complementary tracers in the massive star-forming complex RCW122 (NE & SW)
papers.abstract: AIMS: By combining CH3CCH and CCH, we present a first multi-transition analysis of the RCW122-NE and RCW122-SW regions in the massive star-forming complex RCW 122. The aim is to investigate and to constrain the nature, chemistry, and evolutionary stage of each region. METHODS: We performed observations with the Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX). The analysis is based on 39 CH3CCH lines with J=10-9 to 20-19 (170.8-341.8 GHz) and four hyperfine components of the CCH N=4-3 transition (349.1-349.6 GHz). We estimated excitation conditions using both local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and non-LTE methods, with rotational-diagram analysis and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) calculations. Gas-grain chemical models were performed with the Nautilus code to reproduce the observed abundances over timescales characteristic of high-mass YSO evolution. RESULTS: The excitation analysis of CH3CCH indicates two physical components suggestive of a thermal gradient. The NE region yields T~41-61 K and N_tot~1x10^{16} cm^{-2}, while SW exhibits T~33-48 K and N_tot~7x10^{15} cm^{-2}. In both regions, CCH traces cold gas below 15 K with an H_2 density of 0.5-4x10^6 cm^{-3}. The detection of the ^{13}C isotopologues of CCH indicates that C^{13}CH is more abundant than ^{13}CCH. Chemical models at various evolutionary stages, with cosmic rays as a key parameter, reproduce the observed CCH and CH3CCH abundances, although the two species form through chemically distinct routes. CONCLUSIONS: We provide a coherent scenario in which CCH traces colder gas at an early evolutionary stage, whereas CH3CCH traces a region characterized by a warmer temperature gradient, associated with chemically more evolved gas at a later stage. These results constrain the conditions governing the origin and survival of interstellar species in a thermally and chemically stratified medium.

papers.title: Central charges as black-hole hair in weakly coupled trace-anomaly gravity
papers.abstract: We study black holes in Gabadadze's weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, keeping both the Euler and the Weyl central charges. We prove that a constant anomalyon on any Ricci-flat geometry, the Kerr family included, solves the full theory if and only if the two central charges coincide. Otherwise, the black holes continuously connected to this branch carry scalar hair whose charge is fixed by the surface gravity, the horizon topology and the difference of central charges alone: maximally supersymmetric matter leaves black holes bald, the Standard Model and photon-dominated sectors produce hair of definite sign, and conformal collider bounds confine it to a universal window. Electric charge separates the two anomaly invariants: the hair reverses sign at a critical charge-to-mass ratio set by the ratio of central charges, its extremal value retains only the Weyl charge, and the Euler charge governs the near-horizon growth of the anomalyon. For every unitary matter sector, the hair regular at the event horizon diverges at the Cauchy horizon. Finally, once the higher-derivative Weyl operator is order-reduced, the background, the anomalyon-graviton mixing and all propagation speeds depend only on the difference of central charges, which extends the no-ghost and Laplacian stability conditions to the full anomaly.

papers.title: Detecting Frame Dragging Effect with Next-Generation Spaceborne Clocks in a LEO-DRO Satellite Configuration
papers.abstract: Our approach employs a satellite constellation comprising one satellite in low Earth orbit (LEO) and one satellite in distant retrograde orbit (DRO). This configuration is designed to enhance the sensitivity to the Earth's rotation-induced frame-dragging signal while providing a stable and gravitationally isolated frequency reference. We derive a complete relativistic formulation for the frequency comparison between LEO and DRO, incorporating the post-Newtonian metric, higher-order Earth multipoles, lunar and solar tidal potentials, and the gravitomagnetic vector potential. The frame-dragging signal is of order $10^{-20}$, a level that is becoming increasingly accessible with next-generation optical clocks. Recent advances in zero-dead-time strontium optical lattice clocks have demonstrated a fractional frequency instability of $2.9\times10^{-19}$ at an averaging time of 20,000~s, with an estimated one-day stability of $2.5\times10^{-19}$. With continued advances in clock stability, achieving fractional-frequency sensitivity at the $10^{-20}$ level appears feasible in the near term, potentially enabling the direct measurement of a frame-dragging signal of the same order. Such a measurement would constrain Earth's gravitomagnetic field, enabling future investigations of gravitomagnetic effects on Einstein clock synchronization.

papers.title: The system initial mass function of Orion OB1b from probabilistic Gaia DR3 memberships
papers.abstract: [ABRIDGED] Context: Whether the initial mass function (IMF) varies with environment remains a central question in star formation. The multiple populations of Orion OB1b provide an ideal laboratory to test possible IMF variations. Aims: We aim to characterise the stellar populations of Orion OB1b by identifying its constituent groups, assigning membership probabilities to individual sources, and determining their IMFs. Methods: Using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, we identified stellar groups through clustering analysis and assigned membership probabilities with a probabilistic mixture model. Stellar masses were derived from extinction-corrected photometry using pre-main-sequence evolutionary models. Results: We identified eight kinematically distinct groups and a non-clustered population, deriving ages and IMFs spanning ${\sim}0.08$--$10\,M_\odot$ for six groups, all consistent with being gravitationally unbound. Each IMF was fitted with a lognormal distribution below $1M_\odot$ and a power law above. The high-mass regime is statistically indistinguishable across all groups, while four groups also exhibit consistent IMFs over the full mass range. The remaining two groups show differences that may reflect membership uncertainties rather than intrinsic IMF variations. The combined IMF is characterised by $m_c=0.27^{+0.02}_{-0.02},M_\odot$, $\sigma=0.45^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$, and $\Gamma=1.85^{+0.16}_{-0.14}$. The non-clustered population exhibits a broader and more uncertain IMF, although residual field contamination cannot be ruled out. Conclusions: Our results support previous evidence for the complex internal structure of OB1b. The IMF in OB1b appears broadly consistent across its kinematically distinct groups and compatible with other young populations in Orion.

papers.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
papers.abstract: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dot{\phi}^2=\gamma H^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

papers.title: An Intergalactic medium centred parametrisation of the 21-cm power spectrum from the Epoch of Reionization
papers.abstract: The 21-cm signal from the intergalactic medium (IGM) is a key probe of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). In this work, we present a model of the 21-cm power spectrum centred on the state of the IGM. The framework combines aspects of perturbation and percolation theory to deduce a physically informed parametrisation of the power spectrum. Moreover, it complements classical interpretation methods, centred on modelling the properties of the first ionising sources. We define the IGM parameters driving the shape and amplitude of the 21-cm signal, from the globally averaged volume- and mass-weighted ionisation fractions ($\bar{x}_{HII}$ and $\bar{x}_{HIIm}$), the clustering of sources, through the halo bias ($b_{\mathrm{h}}$), and the characteristic sizes of ionised regions ($R_{i}$) and neutral islands ($R_{n}$). We extend this analysis to model the redshift dependence of the power spectrum, constraining parameters such as the midpoint and duration of reionization. We test the IGM framework on three reionization simulations (C2-Ray, 21cmFAST, and POLAR) with varying cosmologies, astrophysics, and numerical assumptions. The framework constrains the IGM parameter space, recovers the midpoint and duration of the EoR as well as the minimum mass of halos hosting ionising sources $M_{\mathrm{min}}$, and the redshift evolution of the global ionisation fraction, the evolution of ionised and neutral regions (measured with the radial mean free path method by Georgiev et al. (2026b, submitted)). Moreover, the IGM framework lends itself to joint analysis with other EoR probes, such as high-redshift galaxies and quasars and the Cosmic Microwave Background.

papers.title: Radial mean free path bubble size distribution (RMFP-BSD) from the Epoch of Reionization
papers.abstract: Among the many statistics used to characterise ionised regions during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), we introduce one which, while closely related to the mean free path bubble size distribution method from Mesinger et al. 2007, is analytically tractable and substantially less dispersive than that method. The radial mean free path (rmfp) method casts six rays along the Cartesian axes in a 3D volume from a random origin to a neutral hydrogen island. This allows us to better quantify the role of overlap during the EoR, identify isolated or interconnected clusters in the simulation, and study the characteristic peak in the ionisation power spectrum, which is important for 21-cm studies of the intergalactic medium. Moreover, we find the method informative about the properties of neutral H I islands during the final phases of the EoR. We also show that applying both methods in tandem can further improve our insight into the morphology of reionization.

papers.title: Joint Flow-Matching Posteriors for Overlapping LISA Galactic Binaries
papers.abstract: Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe millions of galactic binaries (GBs) at once, thousands of them resolvable, with signals that overlap in frequency. We adapt recent advances in large-scale diffusion models, flow matching with a multimodal transformer, to learn the joint posterior once and then draw from it in a fraction of a second. We demonstrate that the approach is scalable to up to 15 653 sources fitted simultaneously, evaluating calibration and coverage w.r.t. the MCMC baseline. The results show that this approach could be realistically scaled to tackle the full global fit problem.

papers.title: Extragalactic carbon-monoxide (CO) as a CMB foreground: an analytic halo model for the CO auto-spectrum and its correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background
papers.abstract: Context. Carbon Monoxide (CO) lines emitted by star-forming galaxies are redshifted into the frequency bands of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) experiments. Their correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background (CIB) may be a non-negligible small-scale foreground. Aims. We develop an analytic, full-shape halo model framework for the CO auto-spectrum and for the CO$\times$CIB cross-spectrum in CMB bands, and assess its impact on current and future high-resolution CMB experiments. Methods. We use a luminosity-weighted halo model with separate occupation distributions of central and satellite galaxies for CO and CIB emitters, CO transitions up to $J=13$, and all auto- and cross-frequency spectra. At $\ell=3000$, the CO$\times$CIB contribution to the sky power is 0.4, 0.7, and 1.9 $\mu$K$^2$ at 90, 150, and 220 GHz, and the CO auto-spectrum is $\simeq0.02\,\mu$K$^2$. papers.title: Preliminary evidence for a Universal Magnetic Field Configuration in Disk-Galaxy Halos with POSSUM
papers.abstract: We use the POSSUM catalog with its high density of background RM sources (30-50 per square degree) to extend previous LOFAR work and investigate the sign of galactic halo magnetic fields. We are searching for the universal configuration that arises if halo magnetization originates from a central Cosmic Battery, and is subsequently transported outward by large-scale outflows. Our analysis considers 10 edge-on galaxies in the field of view of the POSSUM survey with angular sizes between 60 and 100. For each such galaxy we collect all available background RM sources in a circular region with a radius of 2? around it. We rescale all galaxy sizes and their associated background RM source distances to a common galaxy size of 100 and stack all these regions together. We divide the stacked configuration of RM sources into the four quadrants on either side of the stacked galaxy axis. The mean RM of background sources is computed in each quadrant, and we obtain a pattern of positive and negative mean RM values around the stacked galaxy. A consistent, systematic RM-gradient pattern emerges inside about 6 stacked galactic radii, as expected in Magnetic Disk-Winds with the axial magnetic field configuration predicted by the Cosmic Battery. The inferred large-scale axial electric current in the halo flows from the center outwards. Beyond 6 galactic radii we observe the reverse mean RM pattern, as expected in the axial Magnetic Black-Hole Jet configuration predicted by the Cosmic Battery. Our work confirms the prediction of the Cosmic Battery, and presents one of the very few known signatures of the magnetic field in the halo and the circumgalactic medium (CGM).

papers.title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid
papers.abstract: Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. Matching the local Schwarzschild corrections to a global Green tensor identifies the leading source coefficients. Reflection makes these coefficients equal, and varying the common radial position of the centers makes them vanish. A radial Green function and the heat equation on the sphere determine the angular variation of the lapse and the geometry of its maximum set.

papers.title: Lyapunov Stability of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by the Kiselev Anisotropic Fluid
papers.abstract: We investigate the geodesic structure and the stability of circular orbits around a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a Kiselev anisotropic fluid, characterised by the equation-of-state parameter $\omega$ and the normalisation parameter $N$. We consider six representative values, $\omega=-1,-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3$ and $1$, over the admissible range of $N$ determined by the horizon structure, including the corresponding extremal limits. Using the effective potentials for null and timelike geodesics, we determine the photon sphere, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and the outermost stable circular orbit (OSCO), and examine their stability through coordinate-time Lyapunov exponents. The photon sphere is unstable for all values of $\omega$ and $N$ considered. Its instability weakens with increasing $N$ for $\omega\leq0$ and vanishes at extremality for $\omega=-1$ and $-2/3$, whereas it varies non-monotonically with $N$ for $\omega=1/3$ and strengthens for $\omega=1$. For $\omega=-1$ and $-2/3$, stable circular orbits are confined between the ISCO and the OSCO, which merge at a critical value of $N$ beyond which no stable circular orbits exist. In contrast, for $\omega\geq-1/3$ stable circular orbits exist at all radii beyond the ISCO, whose location varies with $N$. We also derive a closed-form expression for the squared coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent $(\lambda_t^T)^2$, valid for arbitrary $\omega$, whose sign changes exactly at the ISCO and OSCO, so that the Lyapunov criterion reproduces the boundaries of stable circular motion. The Schwarzschild--de Sitter, mass-shifted Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström geometries are recovered as special cases, and the results may have implications for black-hole shadows, thin accretion discs and quasi-periodic oscillations.

papers.title: Closure of averaged Einstein equations by DESI data
papers.abstract: We benchmark the hypothesis that the redshift dependence of postulated dark energy in the standard model, measured by the DESI collaboration, is a natural outcome of dark energy-free models of structure formation in general relativity. We recall fundamental results and the properties of averaged dust cosmologies that suggest to replace the dark energy equation of state through the nonperturbative impact of the inhomogeneous geometry. The relevant mechanism can be phrased in terms of an effective mean field description of inhomogeneities using the fluid analogy of a scalar field (the `morphon'). Without violating energy conditions this effective field exhibits a cross-over to phantom behaviour, compatible with observations. The exact dark energy-free framework needs a single closure condition that we implement in terms of parametrizations of the 3-years data of the DESI team. The resulting redshift dependence of effective cosmological characteristics is then illustrated and subject to physical interpretation. The aim of this paper is to set a benchmark that has to be met by any structure formation model or simulation investigated within general relativity in a flow-orthogonal foliation of spacetime, given the hypothesis.

papers.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.

papers.title: A hybrid effective field theory description of diffuse baryons
papers.abstract: Galaxy feedback mechanisms that displace baryonic gas on large scales are a dominant uncertainty in many cosmological analyses. Measurements that directly probe the baryonic component, such as Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure (FRB DM) and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect, can therefore be used to place constraints on feedback and inform other analyses, such as weak lensing. Thus far, analytic methods to model the effects of feedback are either limited to large scales, missing the regime of high signal-to-noise, or have many parameters, weakening constraining power. We propose a Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT) approach, relying on the full gravitational displacement field computed in an $N$-body simulation. We account for feedback via a Lorentzian suppression with a single effective parameter, $c_f^2$. To describe the diffuse baryon field, we extend the arguments by Andrew et al. (arXiv:2604.25828), leveraging most baryons being in a diffuse state to reduce a full bias expansion to just the linear bias, $b_{1,d}^L$. With just these two parameters, we fit the diffuse gas power spectrum in most variants of the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological simulations at percent-level accuracy out to $k=1\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at redshift $z=0.5$ and $k=1.5\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at $z=1$. Further, by fitting the diffuse gas power spectrum including terms argued to be negligible, we show that their contribution is minimal. Applying this prescription for diffuse electron gas enables constraints on both cosmology and astrophysics without the need to marginalize over many unknown parameters.

papers.title: On the effect of a redshift- and metallicity-dependent top-heavy IMF on high-redshift UV luminosity functions
papers.abstract: JWST observations have revealed a higher-than-expected abundance of bright galaxies at $z \gtrsim 10$. Several scenarios have been proposed to explain this excess, one of which invokes a top-heavy stellar initial mass function (IMF) in the early Universe. In this work, we construct spectral energy distribution (SED) templates based on a redshift- and metallicity-dependent IMF ($z$-$Z$ dependent IMF) motivated by the star-cluster simulations of Chon et al. (2022) and the redshift-dependent IMF model of Steinhardt et al. (2020). We implement these templates in a semi-analytic galaxy model built on a large-box $N$-body simulation to investigate the impact of a top-heavy IMF on the ultraviolet luminosity function (UVLF) of high-redshift galaxies. The adopted $z$-$Z$ dependent IMF enhances the UV luminosity of young stellar populations, particularly at low metallicity, and increases the scatter in the UV luminosity-to-star formation rate conversion factor relative to the Kroupa IMF. Without dust attenuation, both top-heavy IMF models predict a substantially enhanced bright end of the UVLF. However, when dust attenuation is included and calibrated at $z=7$, IMF-dependent metal enrichment and the resulting dust attenuation partly offset the intrinsic UV enhancement. The self-consistent model broadly reproduces the observed UVLF at $z\sim10$, although discrepancies remain at $z\gtrsim12$. For the selected high-redshift UVLF constraints, the best-fitting dust optical depths are 51% and 21% of the fiducial values at $z=9.7$ and $13.04$, respectively, indicating a preference for weaker effective dust attenuation. The highest-redshift comparison does not provide a robust constraint. Our results highlight the importance of accounting for both enhanced stellar UV emission and IMF-dependent metal enrichment and dust attenuation when assessing the impact of a top-heavy IMF on high-redshift galaxies.

papers.title: Interpretable morphology-based marked statistics
papers.abstract: The shapes and environments of cosmic structures carry cosmological information beyond the matter power spectrum. Recovering this information while retaining a physical understanding is a central challenge for cosmological inference. We construct an interpretable, rotation-equivariant neural marking scheme that reweights the matter field, combining learned density responses with explicit measures of local morphology. This approach enables direct inspection of the learned transformations, while retaining the advantages of a two-point function analysis. We employ a contrastive learning framework to align the marked summaries with the respective cosmological parameters. In real-space matter simulations, the learned marked spectra recover information beyond the ordinary power spectrum, tightening marginalized Fisher constraints on $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_m$ by factors of $1.7\times$ and $1.5\times$ relative to the power spectrum plus bispectrum at $k_{\mathrm{max}}=0.3\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Without retraining, our mark also improves a neutrino-mass forecast by a factor of $1.5\times$ relative to the power spectrum at the same scale cut. Across the cosmological prior, our marking scheme also improve the prediction errors in both parameters by $1.3\times$ over the best tested classical mark at $k_{\mathrm{max}}=0.2\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. A qualitative comparison with neural forecasts motivates the possibility that these different compressions approach a common information level. Neural marked statistics thus offer a route to extracting non-Gaussian information from cosmological surveys, combining interpretable, physically motivated transformations with the practical advantages of two-point estimators.

papers.title: Enhancing eccentricity through tidal resonance in binary neutron star systems
papers.abstract: Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. Since binaries formed in isolation are expected to circularize long before merger, measurable eccentricity suggests dynamical formation in dense stellar environments. However, using numerical-relativity simulations, we show that eccentricity can be introduced in the late inspiral of an initially quasicircular binary, due to the $f$-mode resonance of one of the stars. We simulate the merger of two highly spinning neutron stars, one star spinning prograde and the other retrograde. Persistent tidal resonance with the $f$ mode of the retrograde-spinning star is observed, accompanied by a gradual change of its spin due to angular momentum transfer from the orbit. This spin change can be well explained by a simple resonance locking model that accounts for the spin-dependent shift of the $f$-mode frequency. These findings reveal an origin of eccentricity in binary neutron stars that is independent of their formation history and provide important information for modeling binary neutron star dynamics with rapidly spinning stars.

We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.

papers.title: On the existence of constants of motion for multipolar test-body dynamics
papers.abstract: We show that the conservative equations of motion of an extended test body, with force and torque sourced by spin-induced and adiabatic tidal multipoles of arbitrary order, are the flow of the Hamiltonian $H=-\tfrac12\mu^2+\mu U$, where $\mu$ is the body's kinematic mass and all multipoles enter through a covariant scalar potential $U$. For such bodies, a certain notion of mass and a spin norm are shown to be exactly conserved, at all multipolar orders and in any background. We then apply our framework to the Kerr spacetime, and construct extensions of the Carter and Rüdiger constants through hexadecapolar order (quartic in spin). They are found to exist if, and only if, the body's multipoles are those of a Kerr black hole. Together with the energy and angular momentum, they make the dynamics of a spinning test black hole in Kerr perturbatively integrable through that order. Lastly, at the next, quintic-in-spin order, an analytic criterion implemented numerically reveals that neither constant admits a continuation, for any conservative multipoles. In the conservative, test-body limit, black-hole binaries thus carry a dynamical hidden symmetry shared by no other compact objects, which persists to high multipolar order but ultimately breaks.

papers.title: The Simons Observatory: Analysis of methods for polarization calibration of multiple instruments

The relative-angle uncertainty is $\sim 0.1^\circ$ for $\ell_{\max}^{\mathrm{SAT}}=300$, improving to $\sim 0.04^\circ$ at $\ell_{\max}^{\mathrm{SAT}}=600$, subject to SAT beam and transfer-function control. papers.title: Horizon mergers and initial test-charge acceleration in charged black-hole geometries with anisotropic sources

Using a common mass-function formulation, we derive the horizon-merger conditions and classify the Kiselev branches. In this family, the inner-event merger charge provides only an upper bound: three distinct positive horizons can additionally require a positive lower charge bound associated with the event-cosmological merger. For a test particle released from rest relative to a static observer, we derive the local charge-to-mass threshold for outward initial acceleration. Writing $\lambda=q/\mu$ and $z=Q/Q_{\rm ext}$, where $Q_{\rm ext}$ is the inner-event merger charge, the subextremal string-cloud threshold has infimum $1/z$, approached only at infinity. For the subextremal logarithmic profile, the threshold exceeds unity throughout the finite exterior and attains a finite global minimum. For $\alpha/M=0.4$ and $Q/M=1.2$, this minimum is $\lambda_*\simeq1.251125$. In a nondegenerate Kiselev static patch, the neutral balance radius is unique and radially unstable. Density matching supplies conditional profile normalizations, not observational fits. For the logarithmic profile, the integration parameter is distinguished from the mass combination inferred from circular motion. These results characterize geometric horizon bounds and test-particle dynamics; they do not establish a two-black-hole force law or a mechanism for cosmic acceleration, nor do they constitute a test of the Weak Gravity Conjecture.

papers.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
papers.abstract: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $\phi_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $\phi_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. papers.title: The FRB Population Revisited: Rate, Energy, Evolution, and Host-DM Constraints from the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
papers.abstract: We present a study that simultaneously fits for key fast radio burst (FRB) population properties using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog while calibrating for instrumental selection effects. Our inferred volumetric rate at $z=0$ is $1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\times 10^{5}\,{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ above an isotropic-equivalent energy of $10^{39}$ erg and below a scattering timescale of 30 ms at 600 MHz. The evolution of the FRB rate relative to the cosmic star formation rate remains statistically unconstrained. Assuming a Schechter function for the energy distribution, isotropic emission, and 1-GHz emission bandwidth, we find a characteristic maximum energy of $2.0^{+2.6}_{-1.0} \times 10^{41}$ erg and a differential power-law index of $-1.41\,^{+0.27}_{-0.21}({\rm stat.})\,\pm\,0.35({\rm sys.})$. The host galaxy contribution to the observed dispersion measure (DM) is modeled as a log-normal distribution; assuming a total Galactic contribution of 80 $\text{pc cm}^{-3}$, we find a median host-galaxy DM contribution of $199^{+34}_{-36}\;\text{pc cm}^{-3}$ in the rest-frame. Finally, we find that the average FRB spectrum, described by a spectral index of $\alpha=-1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$, is inconsistent with being flat at the $\sim2\sigma$ level. We note an excess of high-S/N bursts at low DMs in the observed sample that is not predicted by the best-fit model. Testing alternative models does not alleviate this tension; future population studies may mitigate this limitation by incorporating robust fluence and redshift measurements.

papers.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
papers.abstract: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $\gamma = 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $\delta\Phi_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.

papers.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
papers.abstract: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints, and identify energy--momentum conservation with covariance of the constitutive Lagrangian. The nonrelativistic limit and a relation of entropy-level helicity to split Calabi--Yau geometry are briefly indicated.

papers.title: Refined, Reliable and Reproducible: Algorithmic Analysis and Reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder
papers.abstract: Cosmic voids are vast underdense regions of the Universe that encode valuable information about its large-scale structure and evolution. By extending spherical voids into overlapping sphere structures, the Popcorn Void Finder demonstrated an improved statistical characterization of cosmic void populations. However, its origin as a research prototype progressively hindered its maintainability and extensibility. Moreover, post-publication algorithmic modifications have not been systematically evaluated, leaving their statistical and computational consequences insufficiently characterized. In this work, we present a comprehensive reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder, prioritizing algorithmic transparency, maintainability, and reproducibility. We document the complete identification procedure, revisit the original algorithmic choices, and evaluate their statistical and computational consequences. Comparisons between implementations revealed a significant change in the behavior of the Void Size Function, which is now characterized by a power-law regime transitioning to a Schechter-like distribution. These changes not only provide a better characterization of void sizes, but enable a new and more robust method to the determination of the shot-noise dominated regime, without implicit dependencies on internal finder parameters present in previous works. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a 1.62x speedup in spherical void identification and a substantial improvement in overlap-removal throughput. We determined the Popcorn algorithm to be negatively affected by load imbalance, and found a speedup of 63x in a tested configuration with a newly introduced early growth termination criterion. These results establish a more maintainable and reproducible foundation for popcorn void identification, while clarifying the statistical and computational trade-offs that govern its performance.

papers.title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
papers.abstract: We validate a subset of the astrometric accelerations reported in Gaia DR3 non-single-star solutions by their consistency with the gravitational pull of known, resolved companions. Cross-matching 338,215 DR3 acceleration solutions against the Washington Double Star (WDS) catalog of visual binaries yields 2,466 unique pairs within 2". For each pair we compare the measured acceleration with alpha_max, the Newtonian bound on the acceleration the companion can impart on the Gaia-tracked photocenter. For 98.1% of the pairs the measured acceleration exceeds this bound by more than a factor of 10, so the cataloged companion cannot be responsible and the perturber must be a closer, unresolved one. The remaining 45 plausible wide binaries are close pairs at the WDS resolution limit. We fit orbits with an updated orvara, extended to accept the DR3 acceleration and jerk coefficients as direct constraints and released with htof as part of this work. The fits converge for 16 of the 45 and one boundary case, the rest having too few resolved measures or a perturber other than the cataloged pair, and 13 of the 17 carry enough data to test the coefficients. Eleven of the 13 statistically accommodate the reported accelerations, for seven- and nine-parameter solutions alike, and the dynamical companion masses agree with the photometric estimates where the photocenter conversion is well determined. Independently of the fits, 33 of the 43 plausible systems with a usable position angle (77%) have the acceleration directed within 45 degrees of the primary-companion axis, against 50% for a control sample: DR3's measured accelerations point in the directions of the cataloged companions.

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.

papers.title: Sound of Keplerian binaries in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background
papers.abstract: We formulate the dissipation due to sound-wave emission from a Keplerian binary embedded in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background at rest in the binary center-of-mass frame within linear perturbation theory. Rather than starting from the local wake force, we treat the binary as a localized periodic mass source and compute the sound-wave fluxes carried away by the medium. The time-averaged energy, linear-momentum, and angular-momentum fluxes are obtained from Noether currents of the fluid perturbations. For a classical inviscid barotropic Newtonian fluid, retaining the self-gravity of density perturbations while adopting the Jeans prescription, we derive explicit flux formulas for circular and eccentric binaries with arbitrary mass ratio. This formulation also clarifies the ultraviolet behavior of point sources: in a nondispersive fluid, the harmonic sum becomes cutoff-sensitive precisely when at least one component becomes supersonic. We examine explicitly how finite source size removes this divergence using a uniform-sphere model and relate the resulting regularization to a corresponding effective harmonic cutoff. The associated secular eccentricity evolution exhibits circularization in the subsonic regime when the fluid self-gravity is sufficiently weak but can change sign outside this regime, with eccentricity growth in the strictly supersonic UV limit. For a Schrödinger-Poisson quantum fluid, quantum pressure instead softens the high-frequency contribution and renders the point-source fluxes UV finite within the nonrelativistic regime; our numerical results further indicate eccentricity growth due to sound radiation over the parameter space explored. Finally, we translate orbital-decay measurements of two binary pulsars into order-of-magnitude bounds on the homogeneous quantum-fluid density surrounding each system.

papers.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
papers.abstract: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about $\pm 30\%$ of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. For the 248 keV event, the accessible inelastic mass splitting is likewise controlled by this tail. Some anisotropic models extend the allowed kinematic region towards splittings at which solar-neutrino constraints on a Higgsino interpretation become ineffective, although kinematic accessibility alone does not establish viability at the fixed Higgsino cross section. These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.

papers.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures through state--operator duality. Using a gravitational charge as a quantum clock, we construct a modular crossed product with density operators whose trace entropy reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time surprisal FT treats the complete channel, identifies the nonunital correction, and yields a GSL bound for unital dressed evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that does not mix distinct dressed-charge sectors and preserves the full dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The entropy bounds establish the GSL in a controlled slow-clock limit and quantify finite-width clock corrections.

papers.title: Modeling the chemical impacts of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes
papers.abstract: Some protostars undergo episodic accretion, resulting in luminosity outbursts that heat their envelopes. The increase in temperature alters the position of the snowlines, which return to their original locations on different timescales depending on the species. However, the chemical effects of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes, including their long-term consequences, remain poorly explored. We investigate the chemical impact of luminosity outbursts on the envelope of a solar-type protostar, accounting for its dynamics, and identify trends in the molecular response relative to both ongoing and past outburst activity. We combined the dynamic semi-analytic code APE with the three-phase chemical model NAUTILUS to predict the time evolution of 83 molecular abundances between 10 and 10,000 au in the collapsing envelope. The outburst was parameterized by increasing the protostellar luminosity by a factor of 100 for 100 years. The outburst shifts molecular snowlines outward by up to a factor of ten, thus enriching the gas phase through thermal desorption. Most species return to their pre-outburst state within a few thousand years at most for r$\leq$1000 au and remain in that state thereafter. However, eight molecules (HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, C2H5CHO, OCS, SO2, C2S, C3S, and HC3N) show abundance deviations 10$-$50 kyr after the outburst in the warm inner regions (T$\geq$100 K), due to the inward transport of chemically altered material. Eight other species (CH3O, C2O, NH2, HCCO, HCNO, HNO, NO, and NCO) show enhanced gas-phase abundances at intermediate radii ($\sim$300$-$1500 au). Overall, most molecules are impacted by outward snowline shifts. With the exception of HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, and C2H5CHO, all complex organic molecules (COMs) are expected to exhibit similar abundances in the warm inner regions of protostars (hot corino), regardless of whether they undergo outbursts.

papers.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
papers.abstract: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,\alpha}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,\alpha}$ is of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$.

papers.title: Pseudoscalar Yukawa Preheating via Effective Action Approach
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate helicity-dependent fermion production driven by a pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction within the one-loop effective action framework. By integrating out the fermionic fields and employing the Schwinger proper time representation, we derive an analytical expression for the fermion pair production probability near each zero crossing of the oscillating inflaton field. We further introduce a helicity transfer matrix to describe the evolution of fermionic modes through successive non-adiabatic production events. For an undamped inflaton background, the temporal symmetry around successive zero crossings leads to the cancellation of helicity-mixing contributions after an even number of events, preventing the accumulation of helicity asymmetry. We then extend the analysis to a damped oscillatory background, in which the decreasing inflaton amplitude breaks this temporal symmetry and modifies the transfer matrix at each crossing. The resulting non-commuting transfer matrices produce a persistent helical spectrum, as demonstrated by the probabilities as a function of momentum obtained after successive scattering events. A comparison with scalar Yukawa preheating further confirms the role of helicity mixing in generating the helical asymmetry induced by pseudoscalar mechanism. These results establish an effective action framework for studying helicity asymmetry during fermionic preheating and provide insight into the influence of the inflaton's dynamical evolution on particle production.
